units.title: A finite real power series
units.statement: A finite set of natural exponents and arbitrary real coefficients define a polynomial by summing the supported monomials.

steps.title: Build the finite sum
steps.text: Evaluate a_j u^j for every supported exponent and add the results. No convergence hypothesis is needed because the support is finite.
steps.lean: The definition is a `Finset.sum`.

units.lean_statement: Lean records the support, coefficient family, and evaluation point explicitly.
units.lean_proof: This is the complete construction, rather than a proof of another claim.
units.boundary: No canonical support or infinite-series statement is asserted.

units.title: The closed formula for every derivative order
units.statement: The order-r derivative expression weights u^(j-r) by the descending factorial j^(r) and the original coefficient.
assumptions: r and j are natural numbers.
When j<r, the descending factorial is zero.

steps.title: Differentiate each monomial formally
steps.text: The r-th derivative of u^j is j falling r times u^(j-r), including the zero case j<r.
steps.lean: `Nat.descFactorial` handles all orders uniformly.

units.lean_statement: The order is explicit and the result is real-valued.
units.lean_proof: The later theorem identifies this expression with Mathlib's actual iterated derivative.
units.boundary: This definition alone does not assert differentiability.

units.title: An absolute coefficient budget
units.statement: Replace each coefficient by its absolute value and retain the derivative's descending-factorial weight.
assumptions: No coefficient sign condition is used.

steps.title: Discard cancellation
steps.text: Summing absolute coefficient contributions produces a point-independent majorant.
steps.lean: The definition is a finite sum of nonnegative real terms.

units.lean_statement: The mass depends on order, support, and coefficients, but not u.
units.lean_proof: It is designed to pair with the hypothesis |u|≤1.
units.boundary: The budget need not be sharp.

units.title: Finite power series are smooth
units.statement: Every finite real power series is continuously differentiable to all finite orders.

steps.title: Use closure of smooth functions
steps.text: Each monomial is smooth; constant multiples and finite sums preserve smoothness.
steps.lean: After unfolding the definition, `fun_prop` applies Mathlib's closure rules.

units.lean_proof: The proof uses only standard smoothness rules.
units.boundary: No infinite-series analyticity claim is made.

units.title: The iterated derivative is the descending-factorial sum
units.statement: For every order and point, Mathlib's iterated derivative of the finite series equals the closed polynomial derivative formula.

steps.title: Commute derivative and finite sum
steps.text: Smoothness lets the iterated derivative distribute over all supported monomials.
steps.lean: `iteratedDeriv_fun_sum` supplies the finite-sum rule.

steps.title: Use Mathlib's monomial formula
steps.text: Each term contributes the descending factorial and lowered exponent.
steps.lean: `iteratedDeriv_pow` gives the exact monomial derivative; ring normalization matches the public definition.

units.lean_statement: This identifies an actual Mathlib derivative, not a merely formal polynomial.
units.lean_proof: The proof reuses Mathlib's finite-sum and power derivative APIs.
units.boundary: Only scalar real polynomials are covered.

units.title: Signed derivative budgets on the unit interval
units.statement: On |u|≤1, every iterated derivative is bounded by its weighted absolute coefficient mass.

steps.title: Insert the exact derivative
steps.text: Rewrite the actual derivative as the descending-factorial finite sum.
steps.lean: Use `iteratedDeriv_finitePowerSeries`.

steps.title: Apply the triangle inequality
steps.text: Discard cancellation and split absolute values across products.
steps.lean: `Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs` proves the finite-sum bound.

steps.title: Use |u|≤1
steps.text: Every remaining power is at most one.
steps.lean: `pow_le_one₀` completes the comparison.

units.lean_statement: Low degrees and coefficient signs remain inside the theorem.
units.lean_proof: The proof combines the exact derivative identity with elementary absolute-value estimates.

units.title: A fourth-order composition budget
units.statement: Bounds on the first four outer derivatives control the exact five-term scalar fourth-order chain-rule expression.
assumptions: The inner derivative values are arbitrary reals.

steps.title: Split the five terms
steps.text: The coefficients 1,6,3,4,1 are the exact one-dimensional fourth-order chain-rule coefficients.
steps.lean: The proof names the five summands.

steps.title: Bound each term
steps.text: Apply the triangle inequality and then substitute |k_i|≤A_i.
steps.lean: `abs_add_le`, `abs_mul`, and monotone multiplication give the result.

units.lean_statement: The numerical coefficients are explicit rather than hidden in a generic constant.

units.title: The ambient exponential map of the unit sphere
units.statement: The sphere exponential formula combines the base direction with a sinc-scaled increment.
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space.
w and z are ambient vectors.
sinc supplies the continuous value at z=0.

steps.title: Rotate in the span of w and z
steps.text: Cosine weights the base direction and sine-over-radius weights the increment.
steps.lean: `Real.sinc` makes this a total formula.

units.lean_statement: Lean defines a total ambient-space map.
units.lean_proof: The later norm theorem states the exact tangency conditions for sphere membership.
units.boundary: Without unit length and tangency, unit norm is not asserted.

units.title: A signed great-circle parameterization
units.statement: The curve uses cos(t‖z‖) and sin(t‖z‖)/‖z‖, with a constant zero-velocity branch.
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space.
t may be negative, zero, or positive.

steps.title: Choose the removable branch
steps.text: Zero velocity gives the constant curve; nonzero velocity gives the signed trigonometric formula.
steps.lean: Lean uses an `if ‖z‖ = 0` branch.

units.lean_statement: The signed parameterization avoids the absolute value introduced by ‖t • z‖.
units.lean_proof: Subsequent theorems prove its smoothness and relation to the exponential formula.
units.boundary: w need not be unit and z need not be tangent for the definition.

units.title: Signed sphere geodesics are smooth
units.statement: For fixed base point and velocity, the signed great-circle curve is continuously differentiable to every requested finite order.
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space.
No unit-length or tangency assumption is needed.
n is any Mathlib differentiability order.

steps.title: Split on zero velocity
steps.text: The zero branch is constant; in the nonzero branch all scalar trigonometric operations are smooth.
steps.lean: `fun_prop` proves both branches after the case split.

units.lean_proof: The only case split handles the removable zero-velocity denominator.
units.boundary: Smoothness alone does not imply the curve lies on a sphere.

units.title: The exponential formula is continuous in its increment
units.statement: For a fixed base point, the ambient sphere exponential formula depends continuously on z.
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space.

steps.title: Compose continuous operations
steps.text: The norm, cosine, sinc, scalar multiplication, and addition are continuous.
steps.lean: After unfolding, `fun_prop` applies Mathlib's continuity rules.

units.lean_statement: The conclusion is ordinary topological continuity.
units.lean_proof: The proof is a direct closure argument.
units.boundary: Joint differentiability in both arguments is not claimed.

units.title: Forward exponential steps equal the signed geodesic
units.statement: For nonnegative time, exponentiating the scaled increment tz equals the signed geodesic at t.
assumptions: Zero time and zero velocity are allowed.
w and z are arbitrary ambient vectors.

steps.title: Handle degenerate cases
steps.text: When t=0 or z=0, both sides reduce to w.
steps.lean: Lean discharges both branches by simplification.

steps.title: Rewrite the scaled norm
steps.text: Nonnegative t gives ‖tz‖=t‖z‖.
steps.lean: `norm_smul` and `abs_of_nonneg` prove the equality.

steps.title: Expand sinc and cancel t
steps.text: For nonzero t‖z‖, sinc becomes sine divided by its argument.
steps.lean: `Real.sinc_of_ne_zero` and field simplification finish.

units.lean_proof: All denominator and zero cases are handled explicitly.
units.boundary: The same equality is not claimed for negative t because the exponential formula uses ‖tz‖.

units.title: A fourth-order certificate for sphere geodesics
units.statement: At a unit base point and nonzero velocity, the first four derivatives have explicit formulas and satisfy ‖γ^(q)(t)‖≤2‖z‖^q for q=1,2,3,4.
assumptions: E is any real inner-product space.
z≠0 selects the displayed closed form.
No finite-dimensional or probabilistic hypothesis is used.

steps.title: Differentiate four times
steps.text: Sine and cosine alternate and each differentiation contributes one power of ‖z‖.
steps.lean: Private `HasDerivAt` lemmas prove every displayed derivative.

steps.title: Bound the two components
steps.text: Use the triangle inequality, ‖w‖=1, and |sin|,|cos|≤1.
steps.lean: Private norm lemmas prove all four uniform envelopes.

steps.title: Return one reusable certificate
steps.text: The public theorem packages four exact derivative witnesses and four bounds.

units.title: Tangent exponential steps remain on the unit sphere
units.statement: A unit base point and an orthogonal increment produce an exponential-map value with exactly unit norm.
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space.

steps.title: Handle zero increment
steps.text: At z=0, the exponential formula is w.
steps.lean: Simplification uses the unit-norm premise.

steps.title: Use orthogonality
steps.text: The cosine and sinc components have zero cross inner product.
steps.lean: Inner-product scalar rules reduce this to ⟪w,z⟫=0.

steps.title: Apply Pythagoras and trigonometry
steps.text: The two squared norms are cos²r and sin²r.
steps.lean: `norm_add_sq_real`, `Real.sinc_of_ne_zero`, and `Real.sin_sq_add_cos_sq` prove the identity.

steps.title: Use nonnegativity of norm
steps.text: A nonnegative real with square one equals one.
steps.lean: Nonlinear arithmetic closes the final scalar step.

units.lean_statement: The theorem gives exact feasibility, not an asymptotic estimate.
units.lean_proof: The proof is the orthogonal norm identity plus sin²+cos²=1.
